correctness.rationale: Pass for the corrected files in repairs/2. The frozen finding and proof explicitly depended on a false universal bound and wrongly treated the computed lower bound as redundant. Gravier et al. p. 4 does print 2|V|/(Delta+1), but subdividing each edge of K5 once gives 15 vertices of maximum degree 4 with an identifying code of size 5 (original vertices give singleton traces, subdivision vertices give distinct pairs), contradicting the claimed lower bound 6. Trace-incidence counting gives 2|V|/(Delta+2), only 7 here. The repair proves nine by upward closure, exhaustive rejection of every eight-set, and the all-point witness. I independently built lines as translates of 1-subspaces, enumerated the closed-trace hitting constraints, verified the claimed 1+36+72 families setwise, and built all exchange edges by common eight-subsets. Replay: python3 branches/independent_affine.py. It reproduced 37 vertices/126 edges with radius/diameter 1/2 and four 18-vertex, 27-edge components of radius/diameter 4/4. The cone follows from flag incidence. Fixing a parallel class, the omitted triples have sums 1 or 2 and only one-coordinate changes connect them. In the displayed Pappus incidence map, writing B-parameters as (u+d,v+e) reduces incidence to d+e=(e-d)^2 in F3; the solutions are (0,0),(1,0),(0,1), giving exactly the three specified edges. The maps are bijections since v-u and u+v are independent coordinates. Affine maps are transitive on flags and ordered noncollinear triples by carrying their corresponding bases to one another. Both point and line codes use closed neighborhoods throughout. The proof is exhaustive only for AG(2,3); it does not generalize to arbitrary orders.
